recognize_zh: IgD 染色中寬大的外套區呈強陽性棕色，裡面有兩個相鄰、IgD 陰性的小生發中心被同一個外套區包住（twinning 雙生發中心），外圍濾泡間區則為陰性，符合透明血管型 Castleman 病。
features: Strong membranous IgD staining of a markedly expanded mantle zone
Two adjacent small IgD-negative germinal centers enclosed within a single mantle zone (twinning)
Additional small IgD-negative foci corresponding to vessels or tiny regressed centers
Sharp boundary between the IgD-positive mantle and IgD-negative interfollicular T-zone at the lower right
Concentric arrangement of cells visible in the largest germinal center
describe_en: IgD immunohistochemistry on a lymph node highlights a markedly expanded mantle zone of small B cells with strong membranous staining. Within this single mantle zone there are two adjacent small, IgD-negative germinal centers (twinning), along with smaller negative foci representing vessels or minute regressed centers. The interfollicular region at the periphery is IgD-negative. The staining confirms that the thickened mantle is composed of naive IgD-positive mantle B cells. Findings are consistent with Castleman disease, hyaline vascular type.

ddx.dx: Mantle cell lymphoma, mantle zone pattern
ddx.vs: MCL cells are often IgD-positive as well, so the discriminator is cyclin D1/SOX11 and CD5 positivity with light-chain restriction in MCL but not in Castleman mantles.
Marginal zone lymphoma cells are typically IgD-negative and grow outside a residual IgD-positive mantle, the opposite of the diffusely IgD-positive expanded mantle here.
Reactive follicles have large, active germinal centers with thin IgD-positive mantles, not tiny atretic centers within broad mantles.
